stem.text: The concentration C of a medication in a patient's blood, in milligrams per liter, during an infusion that settles at 75 milligrams per liter moves toward the settling concentration at a rate proportional to the difference between the settling concentration and C. At time \( t = 0 \) hours, \( C = 65 \). Using k for the positive constant of proportionality, write a differential equation for C as a function of t and state the initial condition.

worked_solution.text: The dependent variable is C and the independent variable is t in hours, so the rate is \( \frac{dC}{dt} \).

Proportional to the difference means a constant multiple of it. With k positive, \( k(75 - C) \) is positive when C is below 75 and negative when it is above, so C moves up toward 75 from its starting value.
The equation is \( \frac{dC}{dt} = k\left(75 - C\right) \), and the initial condition, stated separately, is \( C(0) = 65 \).

options.label: \( \frac{dC}{dt} = k\left(75 - 65\right) \), with \( C(0) = 65 \)
options.derivation: the initial value 65 substituted for C inside the equation, so the rate becomes a constant

options.label: \( \frac{dC}{dt} = k\left(C - 75\right) \), with \( C(0) = 65 \)
options.derivation: the difference written as C minus the level, which with k positive drives C away from 75

options.label: \( \frac{dC}{dt} = 75 - C \), with \( C(0) = 65 \)
options.derivation: proportional read as equal, so the constant k never appears
